deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics: no formulas, derivations or computations. It is part of an administrative or scientific report (Gutachten) addressed to the Hannoverian 'hohes Curatorium', the Göttingen University curators. The report answers a 'hohes Rescript' and a 'gesandtschaftliche Note', a diplomatic note probably connected with J. J. Baeyer's 1861–62 proposal for a Central European arc measurement (Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung). That attribution is inferred from content and date, not stated on the page.

The page continues the previous page's list of foreign triangulations to which the Hannoverian triangulation (Gauss's Hannover Gradmessung of 1820–1848) had already been connected. The previous page lists 1) Danish (Schumacher), 2) French-English via the Dutch (Krayenhoff), 3) Prussian (Müffling), 4) Hessian (Gerling). This page adds 5) Darmstadt, 6) Bavarian, 7) Württemberg and 8) Austrian triangulations, the last reaching Upper Italy and nearly the Turkish border. It states that the desired connection has already been achieved satisfactorily.

The authors then:
- accept the Rescript's account and its conclusion that the planned scientific work need NOT (underlined), contrary to the embassy note, lead to resuming the Gradmessung, i.e. the triangulations;
- regard the triangulation of Hannover as completely solved and closed. They call it the most important basis for the 'higher scientific' (underlined) purpose (Zwecks, also underlined), namely the precise determination of the figure of the Earth;
- acknowledge what has been done for the second basis, astronomical determinations of latitude and longitude. The next page continues with this and argues for extending them using the electric telegraph for longitude differences.

No implicit steps need filling. The geodetic idea behind the passage is standard 19th-century geodesy: triangulation networks plus astronomical latitude and longitude determinations at network points give the shape of the geoid.

results.what: Administrative assessment: the Hannover triangulation (Gauss) is complete and already connected to neighbouring national networks, so no new triangulation is needed. Only the astronomical latitude/longitude basis could be extended.
results.modern_name: Geodetic network connection / arc measurement (Gradmessung) policy; precursor discussions of the Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung (1862)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Hannover triangulation); J. J. Baeyer (Central European arc measurement proposal, 1861)
